newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Extra Brazil gov't coffee sales unlikely - roaster.
newsitem.headline: Extra Brazil gov't coffee sales unlikely - roaster.

text.p: Brazil is unlikely to increase the size and frequency of its auctions of government coffee stocks soon because of the poor functioning of the warehouses where the product is held, a roaster representative said.

Roasters have requested an extra auction by end-June, saying domestic supply is at critically low levels, but this will be difficult to put into practice, said David Nahum, secretary general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (ABIC).
"An additional auction will be difficult to manage," Nahum said after a meeting of members of Brazil's coffee council Monday. "We still haven't received the coffee from the auction before last."
The government earlier this month sold nearly 100 percent of a total of 192,250 60-kg bags offered in two separate auctions.
ABIC, which represents roasters, has called for an extra auction of 200,000 bags this month. But the government plans no further sales until the next official auction, scheduled for July 2.
Government warehouses were taking up to 60 days to deliver coffee bought at auctions, with one of the main problems being the lack of officials to clear the product, Nahum said.
"The problem is the lack of officials, the lack of infrastructure," he said. Coffee bought at an auction in early June was only now beginning to arrive, he added.

The domestic industry was having serious problems finding supply, as the harvest of the 1997/98 crop has only recently begun and any new crop coffee would have to rest 60 to 90 days before being usable, he said.
"We think now is a critical moment, even though the harvest has begun," said Nahum.

Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department a at the Industry and Commerce Ministry, said the department would present a report on warehouses at a meeting of the Brazilian coffee council next month.
Only after this report has been made will the way be cleared for bigger and more regular auctions, Nahum said.
